chunks.arabic_text: رَوَى عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامِ).

translations.en: He narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).
A proponent of irtifa' in doctrine, weak.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitāb al-Duʿafāʾ* identifies ʿAbdullāh ibn Bakr al-Arjānī as a narrator of Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him), classifying him as weak (*daʿif*) due to his elevation in doctrine (*irtifāʾ al-qawl*). This specific defect often refers to the theological tendency to elevate the Imam’s status beyond human limits, a key criterion in Shia hadith criticism for distinguishing between sound transmission and doctrinal bias. His inclusion highlights the rigorous scrutiny applied to narrators not just for memory, but for their theological alignment with Imami orthodoxy.
en.seo_question: Who is Abdullah ibn Bakr al-Arjani and what is his status as a narrator?

key_terms.مَرْفُوعُ الْقَوْلِ: A proponent of irtifa' (elevation) in doctrine, often referring to the Qaramita or Ismailis who elevated their imams.
key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ: Weak, referring to the reliability of the narrator in hadith sciences.
key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a common kunya for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
